recipes.name: Kimchi Fried Rice
steps: Chop kimchi and reserve a spoon of its juice. Dice onion; mince garlic.
Saute onion and garlic in oil. Add kimchi and cook until softened and fragrant.
Add cold day-old rice and kimchi juice. Stir-fry on high heat until hot and slightly crispy in spots.
Season with soy and sesame oil. Top with a fried egg and sliced scallion.

steps.name: Bulgogi
steps: Slice: Freeze beef slightly for 20 minutes, then slice very thin against the grain (ribeye or sirloin works well).

Marinade: Mix 4 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 4 minced garlic cloves, grated onion or pear, black pepper, and optional grated ginger. Toss with beef. Marinate 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Cook: Heat a grill pan or skillet very hot. Cook beef in a single layer in batches so it sears, not steams, 1–2 minutes per side.
Rest: Let rest briefly. Optional: cook sliced onion in the same pan until soft.
Serve: With rice, lettuce wraps, ssamjang, and banchan. Wrap meat in lettuce with garlic and sauce.

steps.name: Korean Fried Chicken
steps: Prep: Cut chicken into pieces. Optional: brine in salted water 30 minutes; pat dry.
First coat: Dust with starch or a light flour-starch mix. Rest 5 minutes.
First fry: Fry at 325F (160C) until cooked through but pale, 5–7 minutes. Drain and rest 5 minutes.
Second fry: Raise oil to 350–360F. Fry again until deep golden and very crisp, 2–3 minutes.
Glaze: Mix gochujang, soy, garlic, sugar, and a little vinegar or corn syrup. Simmer until sticky. Toss hot chicken in glaze.

steps.name: Galbi Jjim
steps: Ribs: Soak short ribs in cold water 30–60 minutes to draw out blood; drain. Optional: blanch once and rinse.
Braise liquid: Combine soy sauce, sugar, minced garlic, ginger, mirin or rice wine, and water or stock.
Cook: Put ribs and liquid in a pot. Bring to a boil; skim. Add large chunks of carrot, potato, and onion.
Simmer: Cover and cook on low 1.5–2 hours until meat is tender and sauce is reduced. Add vegetables later if you prefer them firmer.
Finish: Optional: add jujubes, chestnuts, or mushrooms near the end. Serve with rice.

steps.name: Bibimbap
steps: Season each vegetable separately with garlic, sesame oil, and salt.
Place over a bowl of rice. Top with a fried or raw egg.
Mix at the table with gochujang to taste.

steps.name: Sundubu Jjigae
steps: Saute kimchi and garlic in sesame oil.
Add stock and soft tofu. Simmer.
Crack an egg on top and cook until set.

steps.name: Japchae
steps: Cook glass noodles. Stir-fry vegetables separately.
Toss noodles with soy, sugar, and sesame oil.
Combine with vegetables.

steps.name: Kimchi Jjigae
steps: Saute kimchi and pork.
Add stock and tofu. Simmer until flavorful.
Finish with scallion.

steps.name: Tteokbokki
steps: Simmer rice cakes in a gochujang-based sauce.
Cook until thick and glossy.

steps.name: Haemul Pajeon
steps: Make batter with lots of scallion. Add seafood.
Pan-fry until crisp on both sides.

steps.name: Banchan Spinach
steps: Blanch spinach, squeeze dry.
Season with garlic, sesame oil, soy.

steps.name: Samgyeopsal
steps: Grill thick pork belly slices.
Wrap in lettuce with garlic.
Dip in sesame salt.

steps.name: Doenjang Jjigae
steps: Dissolve doenjang in stock.
Add vegetables and tofu. Simmer.
Finish with scallion.

steps.name: Kimchi Jeon
steps: Mix kimchi with batter.
Pan-fry until crisp on both sides.
Serve with soy dip.

steps.name: Naengmyeon
steps: Chill buckwheat noodles.
Prepare cold broth with vinegar.
Top with cucumber, egg, beef.

steps.name: Ojingeo Bokkeum
steps: Stir-fry squid quickly.
Add sauce and vegetables.
Finish with sesame oil and scallion.

steps.name: Hobakjuk
steps: Cook pumpkin until soft.
Blend with rice porridge.
Season lightly.

steps.name: Bossam
steps: Boil pork with aromatics until tender.
Slice thin.
Wrap with lettuce and kimchi.
